topic: What if the Sun became a black hole?
research_summary: Channel check: 26 Nov 2026 (channel_trends, YouTube Analytics 28 d): 47 subscribers, Shorts 1,815 views / 40.4 % viewed, long-form 57 views / 12.9 % viewed, 1.1 subscribers per 1,000 views; top: flute covers 687 and 475, Haunted Hotel story 505; best explainer reach = personal phone hooks, best retention = Space. Changes made because of it: series follow-ups of yesterday's two explainers (Phone Secrets part 2, Black Holes part 2) with the series promise in scene 2; Shorts about 38-45 s with the payoff before second 22; a story with a different structure and twist from yesterday's. Learning applied: rules 1 (short, payoff early), 2 (viewer's own life), 5 (series promise inside 20 s), 6 (everyday-tech first), 7 (Space second). Timely check: Mars passes Regulus today but the Mars-Jupiter peak (16-22 Nov) and the supermoon (24 Nov) have passed, so no strong free timely hook; slot 2 stays a Space series follow-up. Candidates (/40): (1) what if the Sun became a black hole 33 (follow-up of the 25 Nov black-hole fall; follow_up queued in the queue), (2) why do stars twinkle 28, (3) what if Earth had two moons 28, (4) why is space dark if stars are everywhere 30, (5) what if the Moon were twice as close 29. Winner: (1) - best-retention niche plus a series (Black Holes) and a surprising number (eight minutes). Titles (/50): 'What If the Sun Became a Black Hole? Eight Minutes' 45 (chosen, 50 chars), 'Earth Keeps Orbiting a Black Hole Sun' 41, 'Would Earth Survive a Black Hole Sun?' 40. Thumbnails: A a black Sun with Earth still orbiting and the question (chosen), B a timer showing 8:20, C a tiny black dot. Hooks: 'The Sun turns into a black hole. For eight minutes, nothing changes. Why?' (chosen), 'Earth would keep orbiting. In the dark.', 'There would be no way to see it coming.'. SEO: see data/seo/latest.json for 'what if the sun became a black hole'. Gap: most videos either list apocalypse effects or dwell on the swallowed-Earth myth; this Short gives the eight-minute double delay (light and gravity), the unchanged orbit, and why (mass not size) in under 45 seconds. Claims: (1) Earth's orbit would be unchanged if the Sun were replaced by a black hole of the same mass (NASA Imagine the Universe; ESO educational material; Physicsbunn blog) - VERIFIED; (2) the Schwarzschild radius of one solar mass is about 3 km (2.95 km), far smaller than the Sun's ~700,000 km radius (standard GR; ESO page discusses the scale) - PARTIALLY VERIFIED, figure from standard physics, not quoted in the fetched pages; (3) light takes about eight minutes (8 min 20 s) from the Sun to Earth (NASA) - VERIFIED; (4) changes in gravity propagate at the speed of light (LIGO/Virgo GW170817 measurement, standard GR) - PARTIALLY VERIFIED, no source fetched today, narration says 'travel at the same speed'; (5) the Sun is too light to become a black hole and will end as a white dwarf (stellar evolution, standard) - PARTIALLY VERIFIED; theory vs observation: a Sun replaced by a black hole is a thought experiment. Sources: https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/educators/blackholes/imagine/page26.html https://www.eso.org/public/archives/exhibitions/pdf/es1219_educational.pdf https://blog.richmond.edu/physicsbunn/?p=163 Growth: lever = series follow-up (Black Holes part 2 with the promise in scene 2, next_video what is inside a black hole) and retention (the 'nothing changes for eight minutes' hook, countdown visual); policy check: a physics thought experiment with its own countdown structure, different from the phone explainer and the rules story, theory labelled. Quality gate 82/100.

scenes.text: The Sun turns into a black hole. For eight minutes, nothing changes. Why?
scenes.keyword: Sun turns into a black hole

scenes.text: Black Holes, part two. In this video you'll see what Earth feels, and when.
Light takes about eight minutes to reach us, and gravity's changes travel just as fast.

graphic.headline: 8 min
graphic.caption: light from the Sun to Earth

scenes.text: Then the lights go out, and Earth begins to cool.
But Earth's orbit stays the same. Far away, a black hole pulls exactly like the Sun did.
Why? Gravity depends on mass, not size. Squeezed to three kilometres, the Sun pulls the same.
It can't really happen: the Sun is too light, and will end as a white dwarf.

graphic.headline: Too light
graphic.caption: it will end as a white dwarf

scenes.text: सूरज ब्लैक होल बन जाता है। आठ मिनट तक कुछ नहीं बदलता। क्यों?
ब्लैक होल्स, भाग दो। इस वीडियो में आप देखेंगे धरती को क्या लगेगा, और कब।
रोशनी को हम तक पहुँचने में करीब आठ मिनट लगते हैं। गुरुत्व का बदलाव भी उतना ही तेज़ है।
फिर रोशनी बुझ जाती है और धरती ठंडी पड़ने लगती है।
पर धरती की कक्षा वही रहती है। दूर से ब्लैक होल उतना ही खींचता है जितना सूरज।
क्यों? खिंचाव द्रव्यमान से होता है, आकार से नहीं। तीन किलोमीटर का सूरज भी वैसे ही खींचता है।
असल में ऐसा नहीं हो सकता: सूरज बहुत हल्का है और सफ़ेद बौना बनेगा।
तो धरती अँधेरे में घूमती रहेगी, किसी अनदेखी चीज़ से बँधी। क्या आप उसे आते देखते? नीचे बताइए!
